articles.title: When reality TV becomes too real – and why we can’t look away
articles.summary: In today’s newsletter, a reality TV academic – and former Bachelor contestant – speaks with us about the attachments we form with romance reality participants in the wake of a domestic violence charge against a former star.
body: Leading questions: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do?

Dr Rebecca Trelease is a senior lecturer at Auckland University of Technology’s school of communication studies in New Zealand, and during the first year of her PhD, she was also a participant on The Bachelor New Zealand. She’s been a “massive fan” of reality television since the early Big Brother days, and believes many fans engage with popular culture in a critical, scholarly way – regardless of their formal qualifications. But of her time on camera, and the media coverage surrounding it, she says: “It was really fascinating to see it first-hand, but it was also really awful at times and I wouldn’t recommend it.”

Alyx: Tell me a bit about the media cycle surrounding romance reality shows, and the connections that viewers are encouraged to develop with the cast? Rebecca: In romance reality, in some shows we want to see a main hero looking for love across the season, while in others, we want to see two individuals come together and follow them from meeting at the altar, to “are they gonna stay together at the end?”.

articles.title: Still wielding a chainsaw at 85: the Australians restoring nature in retirement
articles.summary: For a growing band of older Australians, retirement has become an unlikely second act, spent rewilding mountains, counting sea slugs and coaxing damaged country back to life. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: When Susan Downes stepped into the hallway of an old farmhouse for sale in York, Western Australia, she felt an oddly certain sense of knowing. “Oh, this is my house,” the retired GP remembers thinking. There was just one problem: it came with 200 hectares.

Widowed and with her children grown, Downes, then in her 60s, was finally able to act on a long-held wish to move to the countryside. She had imagined something modest: an old house with “a little bit of garden and stuff”. Two hundred hectares was rather more than she had in mind, no matter how charming she found the high ceilings. “I thought, the house is lovely, but I can’t possibly do that.”

But the property had gotten under her skin. Returning for another look two weeks later, she discovered Mount Mackie, a 295-metre hill at the back of the farm where ancient York gums and wandoos had survived about 150 years of grazing. Almost all of the understorey had disappeared. “These magnificent old trees” were all that remained. “I felt a great connection to the land,” she says.
points: For a growing band of older Australians, retirement has become an unlikely second act, spent rewilding mountains, counting sea slugs and coaxing damaged country back to life.

articles.title: Venta review: a humidifier that fixes the worst part of humidifiers
articles.summary: Venta’s evaporative mechanism add cool moisture without mist, mineral dust or disposable filters. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I f you live with forced-air heating, you know that winter can bring chapped lips, dry eyes and waking up with a scratchy throat. A common ultrasonic humidifier attacks the issue with an eye-catching stream of cool mist – and they work well. But as I found out after setting up two of them, they also bring an unwelcome guest: dust.

Minerals dissolved in the water travel with those droplets, leaving a messy residue behind. With two running, it was like an invisible dust storm rolled through every day, raining fine white powder everywhere. It coated furniture, clogged air filters and even choked computer fans. I don’t mind dealing with household dust, but a maddening amount accumulated daily.

Distilled water can fix this issue, but it would also saddle me with the plastic waste, hassle and expense of hauling gallons of water home from the store every week. Instead, I started looking for a different approach and found Venta humidifiers, which use natural evaporation to efficiently humidify air while leaving the minerals behind.
points: Venta’s evaporative mechanism add cool moisture without mist, mineral dust or disposable filters.

articles.title: Squeezy olive oil bottles, Meghan’s pot filler tap and the rise of ‘cheffy’ kit in home kitchens
articles.summary: Social media ‘chefluencers’ and open restaurant kitchens have made chefs more visible and inspired aspirational gadget-buying. The Duchess of Sussex is no ordinary home cook, but when Meghan appeared on Instagram this week at a hob presided over by a special pot filler tap, it spoke to a shift in…
body: While the pot filler is now most often found in luxury residential kitchens, it was reportedly invented in the early 20th century as a functional fixture for commercial kitchens. It joins a wealth of other restaurant equipment to have infiltrated our homes, from squeezy olive oil bottles to stainless steel mixing bowl sets.
At Sous Chef, a UK-based independent speciality food brand, sales of chef presses are up 26%, while sales of chef’s trays are booming, according to Holly Thomson, the company’s food editor.

For Ella Risbridger, author of The Kitchen Book: Good Food for Every Day: “It’s an amazing thing, the blurring of lines between restaurant and home kitchens.” A byproduct of the increasing visibility we have of professional chefs at work, whether via open kitchens in restaurants or “chefluencers” on social media, the utilitarianism and gadgets of restaurant kitchens are increasingly aspirational. This week, in a home tour with Architectural Digest, Julianne Moore showed off her Ikea industrial shelves.
points: Social media ‘chefluencers’ and open restaurant kitchens have made chefs more visible and inspired aspirational gadget-buying.

articles.title: Florence Pugh and Finn Cole Go Red Carpet Official
articles.summary: Supporting Cole at the London premiere of ‘In the Shadows,’ Florence Pugh made a compelling case for a softly, softly approach to complementary couple style.
body: Finally! Florence Pugh and Finn Cole have made it red carpet official. The couple stepped out together at the BFI London Film Festival premiere of Cole’s latest film, In the Shadows, with Pugh taking a break from promoting East of Eden to support her boyfriend. And while they didn’t exactly opt for matchy-matchy dressing, their respective looks spoke to a quietly complementary approach to couple style.

Pugh, who has been delighting in a particularly romantic streak of red-carpet dressing of late, wore a gown from Wiederhoeft’s spring 2027 collection, styled by longtime collaborator Rebecca Corbin-Murray. She accessorized with silver Aquazzura sandals, a Bulgari Wild Pop necklace and high-jewelry earrings, and a constellation of delicate diamond piercings by Maria Tash. Hair by Hyungsun Ju (replete with bow-like half-up half-down style), shimmering makeup by Celia Burton, and nails by nail artist Dawn Sterling (A.K.A. Nailglam ) completed the look sweet and sensual look.
points: Supporting Cole at the London premiere of ‘In the Shadows,’ Florence Pugh made a compelling case for a softly, softly approach to complementary couple style.

articles.title: Forget Ferrari Red: Kim Kardashian Pulls up to the Paddock in Pastel Pink
articles.summary: Supporting Lewis Hamilton at the Singapore Grand Prix, Kim Kardashian opted for a look that brought together body-conscious dressing and a sporty sensibility.
body: Forget Ferrari red. Kim Kardashian is making a case for pastel pink in the paddock. The reality star and Skims founder touched down at the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend to support boyfriend Lewis Hamilton, bringing a little feminine energy to the Formula 1 circuit.

Kardashian opted for a sheer, rose-quartz turtleneck maxi dress from Alaïa’s spring 2024 collection, accessorized with black cat-eye sunglasses and a pink Hermès Mini Kelly replete with silver charms. With its leotard-like underlayer and sheer, sweeping maxi skirt, the look was an interesting amalgamation of Kardashian’s style signatures: body-conscious, sporty, and overtly feminine. A more romantic vibe for the paddock—which tracks, given her more loved-up appearances with Hamilton recently.
points: Supporting Lewis Hamilton at the Singapore Grand Prix, Kim Kardashian opted for a look that brought together body-conscious dressing and a sporty sensibility.

articles.title: A Major Haircut and Movie Star Inspo: Inside Amal Clooney’s Glam at the 2026 Albies
articles.summary: With a fresh, layered haircut and shimmering golden makeup Amal Clooney brought a modern twist to Old Hollywood beauty at the fifth annual Albies.
body: Amal Clooney has always had a certain affinity for Old Hollywood glamour: glossy brunette waves, the luminous skin, the impossibly elegant red carpet appearances alongside husband George Clooney. There’s something of the great Italian screen sirens in her beauty playbook, and for Friday evening’s fifth edition of The Albies, Clooney and her longtime hairstylist and makeup artist Dimitris Giannetos took that inspiration a little further, looking to Sophia Loren.

The Albies, hosted by the Clooney Foundation for Justice at London’s Natural History Museum, featured an audience including Laura Dern, Brad Pitt, Marisa Abela and Myha’la Herrold, and Donatella Versace, who gathered to celebrate individuals fighting for justice and human rights around the world. For the evening, Clooney wore a custom Gucci gown by Demna, its sculptural, off-the-shoulder silhouette covered in shimmering gold sequins with a cascade of floor-length fringe.
points: With a fresh, layered haircut and shimmering golden makeup Amal Clooney brought a modern twist to Old Hollywood beauty at the fifth annual Albies.

articles.title: Giulia Be and Conor Kennedy Are Married! See Her Wedding Dresses by Calvin Klein and Harris Reed
articles.summary: Ahead of her wedding to Conor Kennedy in Rio de Janeiro this weekend, the Brazilian singer-songwriter shared her final fittings at Calvin Klein’s New York atelier and with Harris Reed in London with Vogue.
body: Giulia Be and Conor Kennedy are married! This weekend, the Brazilian singer-songwriter tied the knot with the Kennedy scion in a multi-day ceremony in Rio de Janeiro. On Friday, the couple headed up to Christ the Redeemer for a blessing, before holding their religious wedding today, October 10, in a ceremony at a historic church in the heart of the city. To finish the celebrations, they hosted a reception at a historic mansion in the Jardim Botânico.

And a few weeks before the wedding weekend, Giulia invited Vogue to her final fittings—first, at the Calvin Klein atelier in New York to try on her dress for the blessing. Unsurprisingly, she can hardly contain her excitement. “This has been such a journey,” she says, laughing. “It’s so beautiful, and I’m so excited for you all to see it!”

Not only was she about to see the finished dress she would wear to marry Conor, an associate attorney based in Los Angeles and the son of the late Mary Richardson Kennedy and Robert F. Kennedy Jr., but it was designed by the fashion house where Carolyn Bessette Kennedy once worked—and whose sleek aesthetic she helped make iconic.

articles.title: How to Plan a Spa-Hopping Trip Across Vancouver Island
articles.summary: From floating bathhouses to geothermal hot springs in ancient rainforests, Adrienne Matei journeys across Vancouver Island and finds that wellness is woven into the landscape of British Columbia's wild Pacific coast.
body: I'm sitting neck deep in a hot tub, watching a float plane land. Moments earlier, I was in a cold plunge pool and soon I’ll be scooping handfuls of magnesium-infused salt from a glittering pile and scrubbing the mainland off my skin. I’m at HAVN, a floating sauna experience built on a refurbished naval barge moored in the harbor of Victoria, the biggest city on Vancouver Island in British Columbia —and the first stop on a trip around Vancouver Island that I’m referring to as a spa safari, thanks to the abundance of nature-infused wellness offerings available here.

Today, a number of wellness services have tuned into the island's rugged and sybaritic sides. Having arrived in Victoria, with its British-influence Parliament buildings, hotel high teas, a genteel oceanfront promenade, I booked it straight to HAVN. After rinsing off the magnesium-infused salt, I stopped at its cozy onboard cafe, which invites lingering in a robe and sipping a coffee or turmeric-based wellness elixir. I disembarked feeling purified and ready to keep exploring.
